# The prepared data


Every sample from Nova 250 onwards (NORMAL, BENIGN and CANCER, one row per sample, each row the mean of its scans), as in the explorer's
Cohort and parameter tab, after the peak-shift correction (fat peak moved to q = 14 nm⁻¹) and min-max normalisation (0 at the trough, 1 at the fat peak).
**Left**: ordered by Nova number, smallest at the bottom. **Right**: the same curves ordered by the height of the water peak (the mean of the prepared
curve over q = 20-22), highest at the top, with the water-rich top 15% and the fatty bottom 15% outlined.
Each image has its own colour scale, from the 1st to the 99th percentile of what it shows (yellow high, dark blue low).


::: {#cell-fig-cohort .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print(f"{len(all_names)} NORMAL, BENIGN and CANCER samples from {len(set(map(ne.row_nova, all_names)))} patients, Nova {NOVA_RANGE[0]} onwards")

plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7  # small text so both panels fit side by side on an A4 page
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.9))
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_box_aspect(1)  # square panels
panels = ((axes[0], all_rows), (axes[1], all_rows[all_by_water]))  # left: by Nova number; right: by water peak height
for ax, image_rows in panels:
    covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(image_rows).all(axis=0))
    columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
    low, high = np.nanpercentile(image_rows[:, columns], (1, 99))
    left, right = q[columns][[0, -1]]
    ax.imshow(image_rows[:, columns], aspect="auto", cmap=cmap, vmin=low, vmax=high, interpolation="nearest",
                      extent=(left, right, len(image_rows), 0))
    ax.set(xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)", xlim=(2, right))
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])
    ax.axvline(14, color="white", ls="--", lw=0.8)
for (start, stop), colour, text in (((0, all_part), TOP_COLOUR, f"top {PART}%"),
                                    ((len(all_rows) - all_part, len(all_rows)), BOTTOM_COLOUR, f"bottom {PART}%")):
    axes[1].add_patch(plt.Rectangle((2, start), right - 2, stop - start, fill=False, edgecolor=colour, lw=2.5, clip_on=False))
    axes[1].text(right - 0.4, (start + stop) / 2, text, color="white", ha="right", va="center", fontweight="bold")
axes[0].set_yticks([0.5, len(all_names) - 0.5], [f"Nova {ne.row_nova(all_names[0])}", f"Nova {ne.row_nova(all_names[-1])}"])
axes[0].set_ylabel(f"{len(all_names)} samples")
axes[1].set_yticks([])
# an arrow up the left of the right panel: low water peak (fatty) at the bottom, high (fibrous/glandular) at the top
axes[1].annotate("", xy=(-0.11, 0.9), xytext=(-0.11, 0.1), xycoords="axes fraction",
                 arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color="black", lw=1.2), annotation_clip=False)
axes[1].text(-0.11, 0.07, "Fatty", transform=axes[1].transAxes, ha="center", va="top")
axes[1].text(-0.11, 0.93, "Fibrous/\nGlandular", transform=axes[1].transAxes, ha="center", va="bottom")
fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, bottom=0.1, top=0.97, wspace=0.4)
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

@fig-cohort-parts takes the samples in the top and the bottom 15% of @fig-cohort (right) and averages them separately for each cohort.

::: {#cell-fig-cohort-parts .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
part_means = {label: {} for label in COHORTS}  # label: {part: (mean curve, samples)}
for label in COHORTS:
    for part, members in groups.items():
        chosen = all_rows[members][all_labels[members] == label]
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            part_means[label][part] = (np.nanmean(chosen, axis=0), len(chosen))
part_water = {label: {part: float(np.nanmean(mean[(q >= WATER[0]) & (q <= WATER[1])])) for part, (mean, _) in parts.items()}
              for label, parts in part_means.items()}

covered = np.flatnonzero(np.isfinite(np.vstack([m for parts in part_means.values() for m, _ in parts.values()])).all(axis=0))
columns = slice(covered[0], covered[-1] + 1)
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 3.6), sharey=True)
for ax, part in zip(axes, ("bottom", "top")):
    for label in COHORTS:
        mean, n = part_means[label][part]
        ax.plot(q[columns], mean[columns], color=ne.STATUS_COLOURS[label], lw=1.6, label=f"{label}: {n} samples")
    ax.axvline(14, color="black", ls="--", lw=0.8)
    ax.set(title=f"{part.capitalize()} {PART}% ({'fatty' if part == 'bottom' else 'water-rich'})", xlabel="q (nm⁻¹)",
           xlim=(2, 24), ylim=(-0.05, 1.3))
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 15, 20])
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")
axes[0].set_ylabel("I(q), stretched (fat peak = 1)")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

:::


The fatty bottom 15% looks almost the same in every cohort: its water peak height is
0\.10 for NORMAL, 0\.13 for BENIGN and
0\.12 for CANCER. Fatty scans give little to tell the cohorts apart. The water-rich top
15% differs more: 0\.85, 0\.96 and
1\.07.

::: {.callout-important title="Selecting the top 15% rejects true fatty measurements"}
A scan with a low water peak is not necessarily a bad measurement. Many come from breasts that are genuinely fatty, where the
glandular tissue itself sits among fat, so the beam correctly records mostly fat. By keeping only the water-rich top 15%
we throw these true measurements away, and with them the patients whose breasts are mostly fatty. This changes who is left to
classify, and so affects the overall classification: the result describes water-rich (dense) breasts, not every patient.
:::
